references.text: Here the census of all men from twenty years old and upward is mentioned, which is the same group condemned in Num 14:29.
Confirms the fulfillment of the judgment - none of those mustered by Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sinai remained, for the Lord had said they would die in the wilderness.
The people's complaint (הֲלִינֹתֶם - grumbling) that led to this judgment against them.
Continuation of the same judgment, specifying that their bodies should fall in the wilderness and their children should wander for forty years.
Moses recounts the judgment over the evil generation that would not see the promised land.
Describes the fulfillment of the judgment - the entire generation of warriors died out from the camp until they were gone.
God swears in his anger that those who tested him would not enter into his rest.
God lifted his hand against them to strike them down in the wilderness - refers to this event.
A prophetic warning that Israel will again be led out into the wilderness for judgment, echoing the punishment of wandering in the wilderness.
The New Testament refers to this event and asks whom God was angry with for forty years - those who sinned and whose bodies fell in the wilderness.
Jude reminds us that the Lord saved the people out of Egypt, but afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
Paul refers to the fact that God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
